requirements.original: When the definition is referenced in the same module where it is defined, the module identifier of the module (the current module) also may be used for prefixing the identifier of the definition.
requirements.canonical: When a definition is referenced in the module where it is defined, the identifier of the current module MAY be used as prefix of the definition identifier.
requirements.condition: the definition is referenced in the module where it is defined
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- When the definition is referenced in the same module where it is defined, the module identifier of the module (the current module) also may be used for prefixing the identifier of the definition.

requirements.original: For the latter case, prefixing shall only be used for definitions with global visibility for the module.
requirements.canonical: Prefixing with the identifier of the current module SHALL only be used for definitions with global visibility for the module.
requirements.condition: the definition is referenced in the module where it is defined
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- For the latter case, prefixing shall only be used for definitions with global visibility for the module.

requirements.original: It is allowed to rename a module name during its import.
requirements.canonical: An import statement MAY rename the imported module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- It is allowed to rename a module name during its import.

requirements.original: The new name will be visible only in the importing module.
requirements.canonical: The new name given to a module renamed during import IS visible only in the importing module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- The new name will be visible only in the importing module.

requirements.original: a) An import statement shall only be used in the module definitions part and not be used within a function definition and alike.
requirements.canonical: An import statement SHALL only be used in the module definitions part.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- a) An import statement shall only be used in the module definitions part and not be used within a function definition and alike.

requirements.original: a) An import statement shall only be used in the module definitions part and not be used within a function definition and alike.
requirements.canonical: An import statement SHALL NOT be used within a function, altstep or testcase definition or the control part.

ambiguity.issue: "a function definition and alike" does not list the excluded constructs; the example also shows the control part. Chose all behaviour definitions and the control part.
readings: An import statement SHALL NOT be used within a function, altstep or testcase definition or the control part.
An import statement SHALL NOT be used within a function definition or any other definition outside the module definitions part (e.g. component types, groups' members are allowed).

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- a) An import statement shall only be used in the module definitions part and not be used within a function definition and alike.

requirements.original: b) Only top-level visible definitions of a module may be imported.
requirements.canonical: An import statement SHALL import only top-level definitions of a module that are visible to the importing module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- b) Only top-level visible definitions of a module may be imported.

requirements.original: Definitions which are top-level but invisible to the importing module or which occur at a lower scope (e.g. local constants defined in a function) shall not be imported.
requirements.canonical: An import statement SHALL NOT import a top-level definition that is invisible to the importing module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- Definitions which are top-level but invisible to the importing module or which occur at a lower scope (e.g. local constants defined in a function) shall not be imported.

requirements.original: Definitions which are top-level but invisible to the importing module or which occur at a lower scope (e.g. local constants defined in a function) shall not be imported.
requirements.canonical: An import statement SHALL NOT import a definition that occurs at a lower scope than the module (e.g. a local constant defined in a function).
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- Definitions which are top-level but invisible to the importing module or which occur at a lower scope (e.g. local constants defined in a function) shall not be imported.

requirements.original: c) A definition is imported together with its name and all local definitions.
requirements.canonical: An imported definition IS imported together with its name and all its local definitions.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- c) A definition is imported together with its name and all local definitions.

requirements.original: In particular, importing an enumerated type does not impose the restriction given in clause 6.2.4 on global names defined in the importing module.
requirements.canonical: Importing an enumerated type IS NOT imposing the restriction of clause 6.2.4 on global names defined in the importing module.

ambiguity.issue: EXAMPLE 5 states that in module B (which imports enumerated type MyEnumType) the constant "const MyEnumType enumY" is not allowed because enumerated values restrict global names, which seems to contradict this sentence. Chose the literal text; the example may mean that the clash is only forbidden in the context of the enumerated type.
readings: Global names in the importing module MAY be equal to enumerated values of an imported enumerated type without restriction.

Global names in the importing module MAY be equal to enumerated values of an imported enumerated type, except where the definition is in the context of that enumerated type (then clause 6.2.4 applies).

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- In particular, importing an enumerated type does not impose the restriction given in clause 6.2.4 on global names defined in the importing module.

requirements.original: d) A definition is imported together with all information of referenced definitions that are necessary for the usage of the imported definition, independent of the visibility of the referenced definitions (see clause 8.2.5).
requirements.canonical: An imported definition IS imported together with all information of its referenced definitions that is necessary for the usage of the imported definition, independent of the visibility of the referenced definitions.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- d) A definition is imported together with all information of referenced definitions that are necessary for the usage of the imported definition, independent of the visibility of the referenced definitions (see clause 8.2.5).

requirements.original: NOTE 6: If module C imports a definition from module B that uses a type reference defined in module A, the corresponding information necessary for the usage of that type is automatically imported into module C (see example 6 below in this clause).
requirements.canonical: If module C imports a definition from module B that uses a type defined in module A, the information necessary for the usage of that type IS automatically imported into module C.
requirements.condition: module C imports from module B a definition that references a type defined in module A
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- NOTE 6: If module C imports a definition from module B that uses a type reference defined in module A, the corresponding information necessary for the usage of that type is automatically imported into module C (see example 6 below in this clause).

requirements.original: In particular, if module C imports global value or template definitions (e.g. constants, module parameters, templates) or local definitions (e.g. formal parameters of templates, functions, etc. or constants and variables of component types) of an enumerated type from module B, the enumerated values of this type (i.e. the identifiers) are implicitly and automatically imported to module C. That is, the enumerated values are known when an enumerated value or template is used in module C (e.g. when an actual parameter is passed or a value is assigned to a component variable).
requirements.canonical: If module C imports from module B global value or template definitions (constants, module parameters, templates) or local definitions (formal parameters, component constants and variables) of an enumerated type, the enumerated values of that type ARE implicitly imported into module C and are known when an enumerated value or template is used in module C.
requirements.condition: module C imports value, template or local definitions of an enumerated type from module B
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- In particular, if module C imports global value or template definitions (e.g. constants, module parameters, templates) or local definitions (e.g. formal parameters of templates, functions, etc. or constants and variables of component types) of an enumerated type from module B, the enumerated values of this type (i.e. the identifiers) are implicitly and automatically imported to module C. That is, the enumerated values are known when an enumerated value or template is used in module C (e.g. when an actual parameter is passed or a value is assigned to a component variable).

requirements.original: Note that this implicit importing does not impose the restriction given in clause 6.2.4 on global names defined in module C.
requirements.canonical: The implicit import of enumerated values IS NOT imposing the restriction of clause 6.2.4 on global names defined in the importing module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- Note that this implicit importing does not impose the restriction given in clause 6.2.4 on global names defined in module C.

requirements.original: e) If the referenced definitions are wished to be used in the importing module, they shall be explicitly imported either directly from its source module or indirectly by importing the import statements of a module importing it (see clause 8.2.3.7).
requirements.canonical: A referenced definition that is to be used in the importing module SHALL be explicitly imported, either directly from its source module or by importing the import statements of a module that imports it.
requirements.condition: the referenced definition is to be used in the importing module
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- e) If the referenced definitions are wished to be used in the importing module, they shall be explicitly imported either directly from its source module or indirectly by importing the import statements of a module importing it (see clause 8.2.3.7).

requirements.original: f) When importing a function, altstep or test case the corresponding behaviour specifications and all definitions used inside the behaviour specifications remain invisible for the importing module.
requirements.canonical: When a function, altstep or testcase is imported, its behaviour specification and all definitions used inside it ARE NOT visible to the importing module.

ambiguity.issue: "test case" is used for the TTCN-3 testcase definition; "behaviour specification" is used where the semantic description says "behaviour description".

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- f) When importing a function, altstep or test case the corresponding behaviour specifications and all definitions used inside the behaviour specifications remain invisible for the importing module.

requirements.original: g) The language specification (see clause 8.1) of the import statement shall not override the language specification of the importing module.
requirements.canonical: The language specification of an import statement SHALL NOT override the language specification of the importing module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- g) The language specification (see clause 8.1) of the import statement shall not override the language specification of the importing module.

requirements.original: h) The language specification of the import statement shall be identical to the language specification of the source module from which definitions are imported (see clause 8.2.3.8) provided a language specification is defined in the source module.
requirements.canonical: If the source module defines a language specification, the language specification of an import statement importing from it SHALL be identical to the language specification of the source module.
requirements.condition: a language specification is defined in the source module
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- h) The language specification of the import statement shall be identical to the language specification of the source module from which definitions are imported (see clause 8.2.3.8) provided a language specification is defined in the source module.

requirements.original: If not, the language specification in the import statement is taken as the language specification of the source module.
requirements.canonical: If the source module does not define a language specification, the language specification of the import statement IS taken as the language specification of the source module.
requirements.condition: no language specification is defined in the source module
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- If not, the language specification in the import statement is taken as the language specification of the source module.

requirements.original: If the source module uses however language concepts not being part of that language specification, this causes an error for the import statement.
requirements.canonical: If the source module uses language concepts that are not part of the language specification taken from the import statement, the import statement SHALL cause an error.
requirements.condition: the source module has no language specification and uses language concepts not part of the language specification given in the import statement

ambiguity.issue: "that language specification" most likely refers to the language specification taken from the import statement when the source module has none (previous sentence); it could also refer to any language specification of the import statement.
readings: If the source module has no language specification and uses language concepts not part of the language specification of the import statement, the import statement SHALL cause an error.

If the source module uses language concepts not part of the language specification of the import statement, the import statement SHALL cause an error, whether or not the source module defines a language specification.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- If the source module uses however language concepts not being part of that language specification, this causes an error for the import statement.

requirements.original: i) If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the original module name is not imported and cannot be used for referencing the imported module.
requirements.canonical: If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the original module name IS NOT imported.
requirements.condition: the imported module is renamed in the import clause
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- i) If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the original module name is not imported and cannot be used for referencing the imported module.

requirements.original: i) If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the original module name is not imported and cannot be used for referencing the imported module.
requirements.canonical: If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the original module name SHALL NOT be used for referencing the imported module.
requirements.condition: the imported module is renamed in the import clause
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- i) If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the original module name is not imported and cannot be used for referencing the imported module.

requirements.original: The imported module can be referenced using the new local name only.
requirements.canonical: A module renamed in the import clause SHALL be referenced using its new local name only.
requirements.condition: the imported module is renamed in the import clause
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- The imported module can be referenced using the new local name only.

requirements.original: j) If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the new local name of the module shall be unique in the scope of the importing module.
requirements.canonical: If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the new local name of the module SHALL be unique in the scope of the importing module.
requirements.condition: the imported module is renamed in the import clause
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- j) If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the new local name of the module shall be unique in the scope of the importing module.

requirements.original: NOTE 7: Definitions with the same name defined in different modules are always assumed to be different, even if the actual definitions in the different modules are identical.
requirements.canonical: Definitions with the same name defined in different modules ARE different definitions, even if their actual definitions are identical.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- NOTE 7: Definitions with the same name defined in different modules are always assumed to be different, even if the actual definitions in the different modules are identical.

requirements.original: For example, importing a type that is already defined locally, even with the same name, would lead to two different types being available in the module.
requirements.canonical: Importing a type that has the same name as a locally defined type results in two different types being available in the importing module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.1 -- For example, importing a type that is already defined locally, even with the same name, would lead to two different types being available in the module.

requirements.original: Single visible definitions can be imported by referring to the definition kind and the definition name(s).
requirements.canonical: A visible single definition MAY be imported by referring to its definition kind and its definition name(s).
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.2 -- Single visible definitions can be imported by referring to the definition kind and the definition name(s).

requirements.original: The import of single definitions can be used in combination with imports of groups (see clause 8.2.3.3), with imports of definitions of the same kind (see clause 8.2.3.4), and with imports of import statements (see clause 8.2.3.7).
requirements.canonical: An import of single definitions MAY be combined with imports of groups, imports of definitions of the same kind and imports of import statements.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.2 -- The import of single definitions can be used in combination with imports of groups (see clause 8.2.3.3), with imports of definitions of the same kind (see clause 8.2.3.4), and with imports of import statements (see clause 8.2.3.7).

requirements.original: [ Visibility ] import from ModuleId "{" { ( ( type { TypeDefIdentifier [ "," ] } ) | ( template { TemplateIdentifier [ "," ] } ) | ( const { ConstIdentifier [ "," ] } ) | ( testcase { TestcaseIdentifier [ "," ] } ) | ( altstep { AltstepIdentifier [ "," ] } ) | ( function { FunctionIdentifier [ "," ] } ) | ( signature { SignatureIdentifier [ "," ] } ) | ( modulepar { ModuleParIdentifier [ "," ] } ) ) [ ";" ] } "}" [ ";" ]
requirements.canonical: An import statement for single definitions has the syntax [Visibility] import from ModuleId "{" { ( type {TypeDefIdentifier [","]} | template {TemplateIdentifier [","]} | const {ConstIdentifier [","]} | testcase {TestcaseIdentifier [","]} | altstep {AltstepIdentifier [","]} | function {FunctionIdentifier [","]} | signature {SignatureIdentifier [","]} | modulepar {ModuleParIdentifier [","]} ) [";"] } "}" [";"].
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.2 -- [ Visibility ] import from ModuleId "{" { ( ( type { TypeDefIdentifier [ "," ] } ) | ( template { TemplateIdentifier [ "," ] } ) | ( const { ConstIdentifier [ "," ] } ) | ( testcase { TestcaseIdentifier [ "," ] } ) | ( altstep { AltstepIdentifier [ "," ] } ) | ( function { FunctionIdentifier [ "," ] } ) | ( signature { SignatureIdentifier [ "," ] } ) | ( modulepar { ModuleParIdentifier [ "," ] } ) ) [ ";" ] } "}" [ ";" ]

requirements.original: Import of an invisible definition shall cause an error.
requirements.canonical: An import statement that imports a definition which is not visible to the importing module SHALL cause an error.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.2 -- Import of an invisible definition shall cause an error.

requirements.original: a) The definition to be imported shall be defined in the module from which it is to be imported and shall be visible to the importing module.
requirements.canonical: A single definition to be imported SHALL be defined in the module from which it is imported.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.2 -- a) The definition to be imported shall be defined in the module from which it is to be imported and shall be visible to the importing module.

requirements.original: a) The definition to be imported shall be defined in the module from which it is to be imported and shall be visible to the importing module.
requirements.canonical: A single definition to be imported SHALL be visible to the importing module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.2 -- a) The definition to be imported shall be defined in the module from which it is to be imported and shall be visible to the importing module.

requirements.original: Groups of definitions may be imported.
requirements.canonical: A group of definitions MAY be imported.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.3 -- Groups of definitions may be imported.

requirements.original: The import of groups can be used in combination with imports of single definitions (see clause 8.2.3.2), with imports of definitions of the same kind (see clause 8.2.3.4), and with imports of import statements (see clause 8.2.3.7).
requirements.canonical: An import of groups MAY be combined with imports of single definitions, imports of definitions of the same kind and imports of import statements.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.3 -- The import of groups can be used in combination with imports of single definitions (see clause 8.2.3.2), with imports of definitions of the same kind (see clause 8.2.3.4), and with imports of import statements (see clause 8.2.3.7).

requirements.original: It is allowed to import sub-groups (i.e. a group which is defined within another group) directly, i.e. without the groups in which the sub-group is embedded.
requirements.canonical: A sub-group MAY be imported directly, without importing the groups in which the sub-group is embedded.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.3 -- It is allowed to import sub-groups (i.e. a group which is defined within another group) directly, i.e. without the groups in which the sub-group is embedded.

requirements.original: If the name of a sub-group that should be imported is identical to the name of another sub-group in the same module (see clause 8.2.2), the dot notation shall be used to identify the sub-group to be imported uniquely.
requirements.canonical: If the name of a sub-group to be imported is identical to the name of another sub-group in the same module, the import statement SHALL use the dot notation to identify the sub-group uniquely.
requirements.condition: the name of the sub-group to be imported is identical to the name of another sub-group in the same module
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.3 -- If the name of a sub-group that should be imported is identical to the name of another sub-group in the same module (see clause 8.2.2), the dot notation shall be used to identify the sub-group to be imported uniquely.

requirements.original: If some visible definitions of a group are wished not to be imported, their kinds and identifiers shall be listed in the exception list within a pair of curly brackets following the except keyword.
requirements.canonical: If visible definitions of an imported group are not to be imported, their kinds and identifiers SHALL be listed in the exception list enclosed in curly brackets following the `except` keyword.
requirements.condition: some visible definitions of the group are not to be imported
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.3 -- If some visible definitions of a group are wished not to be imported, their kinds and identifiers shall be listed in the exception list within a pair of curly brackets following the except keyword.

requirements.original: The all keyword is also allowed to be used in the exception list; this will exclude all definitions of the same kind from the import statement.
requirements.canonical: The `all` keyword MAY be used in the exception list of a group import.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.3 -- The all keyword is also allowed to be used in the exception list; this will exclude all definitions of the same kind from the import statement.

requirements.original: The all keyword is also allowed to be used in the exception list; this will exclude all definitions of the same kind from the import statement.
requirements.canonical: The `all` keyword used for a definition kind in the exception list of a group import excludes all definitions of that kind of the group from the import statement.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.3 -- The all keyword is also allowed to be used in the exception list; this will exclude all definitions of the same kind from the import statement.

requirements.original: [ Visibility ] import from ModuleId "{" { ( group { QualifiedIdentifier [ except "{" ExceptSpec "}" ] [ "," ] } ) [ ";" ] } "}" [ ";" ]
requirements.canonical: An import statement for groups has the syntax [Visibility] import from ModuleId "{" { ( group { QualifiedIdentifier [ except "{" ExceptSpec "}" ] [","] } ) [";"] } "}" [";"].
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.3 -- [ Visibility ] import from ModuleId "{" { ( group { QualifiedIdentifier [ except "{" ExceptSpec "}" ] [ "," ] } ) [ ";" ] } "}" [ ";" ]

requirements.original: The effect of importing a group is identical to an import statement that lists all visible definitions (including sub-groups) of this group except of those that are listed in the except specification.
requirements.canonical: Importing a group IS equivalent to an import statement that lists all visible definitions of the group, including its sub-groups, except those listed in the except specification.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.3 -- The effect of importing a group is identical to an import statement that lists all visible definitions (including sub-groups) of this group except of those that are listed in the except specification.

requirements.original: Import statements contained in the group or in its subgroups are not part of this list, only definitions are.
requirements.canonical: Import statements contained in an imported group or in its sub-groups ARE NOT part of the group import; only definitions are imported.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.3 -- Import statements contained in the group or in its subgroups are not part of this list, only definitions are.

requirements.original: It is important to point out, that the except statement does not exclude the definitions listed from being imported in general; all statements importing definitions of the same kind can be seen as a shorthand notation for an equivalent list of identifiers of single definitions.
requirements.canonical: An except specification of an import statement IS NOT an exclusion of the listed definitions from being imported by other imports.

ambiguity.issue: 'except statement' is used for the except specification, which is not a statement.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.3 -- It is important to point out, that the except statement does not exclude the definitions listed from being imported in general; all statements importing definitions of the same kind can be seen as a shorthand notation for an equivalent list of identifiers of single definitions.

requirements.original: It is important to point out, that the except statement does not exclude the definitions listed from being imported in general; all statements importing definitions of the same kind can be seen as a shorthand notation for an equivalent list of identifiers of single definitions.
requirements.canonical: An import of all definitions of the same kind IS a shorthand notation for an equivalent list of identifiers of single definitions.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.3 -- It is important to point out, that the except statement does not exclude the definitions listed from being imported in general; all statements importing definitions of the same kind can be seen as a shorthand notation for an equivalent list of identifiers of single definitions.

requirements.original: The except statement excludes definitions from this single list only.
requirements.canonical: An except specification excludes definitions only from the single list of definitions of the import to which it belongs.

ambiguity.issue: 'except statement' is used for the except specification, which is not a statement.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.3 -- The except statement excludes definitions from this single list only.

requirements.original: a) The group to be imported shall be defined in the module from which it is to be imported.
requirements.canonical: A group to be imported SHALL be defined in the module from which it is imported.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.3.3 -- a) The group to be imported shall be defined in the module from which it is to be imported.
